messages:
janet_acme: Hey team — since yesterday we've been seeing streaming responses from the hosted API that hang for ~8-12s before the first chunk after a long idle (client open for ~7+ mins). After the delay the rest of the stream comes through fine. This is happening through our ALB -> nginx ingress. Repro steps below.

mira: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro and any request ids? Is this only with your ALB + nginx stack or does it happen when hitting the API directly? :thinking:

janet_acme: repro: open a background connection to /v1/chat/stream, wait 7+ minutes, then send a prompt that generates immediate tokens. curl we used: 

```
curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-test' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'
```

Headers show 200 and then no bytes for ~10s then first SSE chunk arrives. Happens for many users behind ALB.

alex: Sounds like an "initial chunk stall" after idle. Two likely culprits: ALB connection reuse + NGiNX buffering / proxy_http_version mismatch, or an HTTP/2 window update race at the edge (Envoy/ALB). Can you share nginx config for the proxying?

janet_acme: nginx config attached (excerpt):

```
proxy_buffering on;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection keep-alive;
proxy_read_timeout 90s;
```

ryan: That proxy_buffering on + Connection keep-alive is suspicious. When upstream uses chunked streaming, nginx may wait to coalesce chunks. Try turning proxy_buffering off and ensure `proxy_set_header Connection "";` so nginx forwards chunked body raw. Also ensure `proxy_request_buffering off;` for POST bodies.

ingrid: Also check ALB idle timeout and downstream keepalives. ALB connection reuse + re-use of a half-closed TCP flow can result in delayed first-byte delivery if the kernel waits for a window update. Are you seeing the stall only after > idle timeout?

janet_acme: We see it after ~7 minutes consistently. ALB idle is 350s (default 60?), we didn't change it.

support_engineer_tom: Quick checklist/workarounds to try now: 
- Set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1;` in nginx and reload.
- Add an explicit small heartbeat from client or server to avoid long-idle reuse: send `\n` or `: ping\n\n` as SSE comment every 60s.
- Increase ALB idle timeout to > 600s if you expect very long idle connections.
- If using Cloudflare in front of ALB, set `send_timeout 0`/disable edge chunk aggregation where possible.

support_engineer_tom: Example nginx snippet we recommend: 

```
location /v1/streams/ {
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 360s;
}
```

alex: For Envoy or ALB with HTTP/2, there's also an issue where a stalled WINDOW_UPDATE can block the response until the peer sends a window update. Workaround: route streaming endpoints over HTTP/1.1 from ALB to backend (disable h2) or ensure keepalive pings are enabled.

ryan: If you can capture tcpdump/pcap around the moment of the stall we can check for TCP-level retransmits / window updates. Also check kernel TCP settings — Nagle and TCP_CORK can coalesce tiny writes. `TCP_NODELAY` on the upstream client socket is helpful.

janet_acme: Will try proxy_buffering off and heartbeat. Quick Q: do you recommend server-side heartbeat or client-side in our SDK?

mira: Server-side is ideal if Redwood can emit a comment byte every 30-60s; otherwise client heartbeat works (send empty prompt or SSE comment) but is hacky.

ops-oncall-bot: action_added: Investigate ALB/nginx idle interaction (ticket: SUP-4821) :eyes:

ingrid: If you want a short-term mitigation from our side, we can enable a tiny server-side keepalive on your tenant that emits `: \n` every 45s for streaming endpoints. I'll escalate to infra if you opt in.

janet_acme: thanks — we'll flip proxy_buffering off and add heartbeat in client tonight and report back. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

support_engineer_tom: TL;DR: initial-byte stalls after long idle are usually proxy buffering or HTTP/2 window/idle interactions. Fixes: turn off proxy buffering, ensure HTTP/1.1 proxied to streamers (or enable h2 window handling), add periodic one-byte heartbeats, and tune ALB idle.

mira: ping me with the tcpdump if the workaround doesn't help, we can run a trace with observability team. :mag:
